_grade: [L] LOCKED external input (v7 extension). Three ADDITIONAL ordinal FIRST-APPEARANCE Carnegie stages of human embryonic primordia, compiled from standard human-embryology references and primary staging papers. They are NEVER adjusted to change a correlation. dev_timing_wide.py treats this table as read-only, concatenates it AFTER the original 7 locked features (dev_timing.json, loaded byte-for-byte and unchanged), and tests corr(DNA-derived schedule, observed stage) at n=10. The table does not depend on gamma in any way.
_provenance: Ordinal first-appearance Carnegie stages (CS) for three additional [V]-master primordia, each pinned from a primary/canonical source BEFORE any correlation was computed: (1) future cerebral hemispheres (telencephalic/cerebral vesicle) CS14 -- Muller F & O'Rahilly R, 'The first appearance of the future cerebral hemispheres in the human embryo at stage 14', Anat Embryol 177:495-511 (1988), PMID 3377191; (2) retinal pigment epithelium first melanisation CS15 -- O'Rahilly R & Muller F (Carnegie staging) with the melanogenesis literature placing the first RPE melanin granules at CS15 (~E33-35), PMID 1927245; (3) first chondrification CS17 -- O'Rahilly R & Muller F, 'Developmental Stages in Human Embryos' (Carnegie Inst. of Washington, Publ. 637, 1987): mesenchymal condensations CS16, chondrification of the first cartilaginous elements CS17-18. Exact day estimates are contextual only and are NOT used in the rank-correlation test.
_method: Each primordium is tagged with the SAME master gene used in feature_atlas_plus, restricted to genuine [V] masters. The three master genes (FOXG1, MITF, SOX9) are all present in the locked morpho_gamma.json table; their gamma is read VERBATIM from that table (never recomputed for the schedule). The model's emergence schedule is argsort(spinodal(gamma)) -- a pure readout of MEASURED gamma. RANK correlation is used so the result is robust to +/-1-stage encoding uncertainty.
_scope_note: These three [V] master->feature links are genuine, not representative. FOXG1 is THE master telencephalon transcription factor for the cerebral hemispheres -- it is literally the gene named in the title of the CS14 staging paper (PMID 3377191); the broad morpho atlas conservatively tagged FOXG1 [F] for the vague feature 'cranium', but for the SPECIFIC feature 'future cerebral hemispheres' FOXG1 is the textbook [V] master. MITF is THE melanocyte/RPE master TF (necessary+sufficient for the pigment lineage; already a [V] master in dev_timing's V_MASTERS set). SOX9 is THE master chondrogenic TF (necessary+sufficient for chondrogenesis); it is tagged [F] in the broad atlas only because there it stands in for the whole 'cartilage/skeleton+otic+feather' program, but for the SPECIFIC feature 'first chondrification' it is the canonical [V] master. These two scope corrections (FOXG1, SOX9) are documented here, not applied silently; verify_dev_timing_wide.py records them.
_frozen: This table is content-frozen; verify_dev_timing_wide.py check #2 pins its sha256, asserts the stages are integers independent of the gamma table (not back-fitted), and asserts the master genes' gamma reproduces the locked morpho_gamma.json values (MITF/SOX9 from byte-for-byte cached promoter sequence -> exact; FOXG1 from a once-re-fetched frozen sequence -> within assembly-version drift, residual recorded).

mitf_rpe_pigment.ref: O'Rahilly&Muller; melanogenesis lit (PMID 1927245): first RPE melanin granules at CS15 (~E33-35)

sox9_chondrification.primordium: first chondrification (cartilage of the first skeletal elements)
sox9_chondrification.ref: O'Rahilly&Muller Publ.637: mesenchymal condensations CS16, chondrification of first elements CS17-18
